**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no documented first-touch-to-first-class flow (induction safety, payment setup, expectation-setting, coach assignment)
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back protocol or exit interview process when members leave
- **Member Pause** – no criteria, duration limits, or re-engagement trigger when someone pauses membership
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression path for coaches (skills, certifications, assessment gates, pay progression)
- **Class Quality Audit** – no systematic way to spot-check coaching standards, member experience, or safety compliance
- **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – critical gap for a UK business; no documented data handling, consent, retention, or breach protocol
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics documented (incentives, tracking, attribution, payout process)
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or framework for proactive retention touchpoints (at 30/60/90 days, post-plateau, low attendance)
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** – no process to capture goals on entry, track progress, or measure transformation outcomes
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – no escalation matrix for member complaints, billing disputes, or safety incidents

- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – likely missing detail on class prep, feedback loops, member communication cadence, and accountability checks

# Executing The Service Menu Build for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your vision.** Pull last month's actual bookings/sales data. Map what people actually buy vs. what you *think* you offer. Your menu should reflect what's profitable and repeatable—not everything possible. Cut ruthlessly.

• **Coach-facing menu first.** Give your coaches a 1-page cheat sheet: "Here's what you can sell, here's the exact script, here's what's included so you don't promise extras." This prevents scope creep and inconsistency. Get their input—they'll spot what actually sells vs. sounds good.

• **Pricing anchor to your best performer.** Identify which service/package has the highest uptake or margin. Build your menu around that as the "hero offer," then tier down (budget option) and up (premium/add-on). Members and coaches will gravitate to the middle anyway.

• **Member-facing = one visual piece, one price list.** Don't over-design. Put it on your website, print 20 copies for the gym, add it to your booking system. Use identical names/descriptions everywhere so you're not explaining inconsistencies. Make price increases *visible* only when you next update (don't surprise people mid-month).

• **Lock it for 90 days, then measure.** Once live, track which offerings sell, which create friction, which drive retention. Adjust in the next cycle. Moving it too often confuses your market and your team.
